slides.title: 16.2.1 Using Traditional Enumerations
keyPoints: An unscoped enumeration gives names to integral choices and introduces its enumerator names into the surrounding.

An unscoped enumeration gives names to integral choices and introduces its enumerator names into the surrounding.

slides.narration: In this part of Chapter 16, use 16.2.1 Using Traditional Enumerations as an engineering claim, not a vocabulary word. An unscoped enumeration gives names to integral choices and introduces its enumerator names into the surrounding scope. It can participate in implicit conversions to integer in ways that are convenient for older interfaces but can also allow accidental mixing with unrelated numeric values. When reading legacy code, identify the intended domain before treating an enum as an arbitrary integer. A stored underlying value may not correspond to a listed enumerator, especially after unchecked deserialization. Validation at external boundaries remains necessary. The named constants improve readability, but they do not automatically make every cast from an integer a valid domain conversion. The graduate-level move is to ask what evidence would make the claim trustworthy: a compiler diagnostic, a runtime value, a preserved invariant, or a boundary that failed cleanly. keyPoints: A scoped enumeration such as enum class State { offline, ready, failed }; keeps its names qualified and does not.

slides.narration: In this part of Chapter 16, use 16.2.2 Using Type-Safe enum class as an engineering claim, not a vocabulary word. A scoped enumeration such as enum class State { offline, ready, failed }; keeps its names qualified and does not implicitly convert to an integer. State::ready therefore communicates both the choice and its domain. Two unrelated scoped enum types cannot be casually compared as if their numeric encodings were interchangeable. Choose an explicit underlying type when a binary interface requires one, and validate any incoming numeric encoding before conversion. Do not serialize an enum by dumping its object bytes and assuming a stable cross-platform protocol. Named choices describe program meaning; wire representation and compatibility need a separate, explicit contract. slides.narration: In this part of Chapter 16, use 16.3.1 Replacing Unrelated Variables with Structured Models as an engineering claim, not a vocabulary word. A collection of Device objects keeps related fields together. This is easier to copy, return, and validate than three vectors whose matching indices must remain synchronized. A function accepting one record can state a coherent requirement instead of relying on callers to pass fields in the correct order. Model only the distinctions that matter to the application. A small teaching record does not need a deep inheritance hierarchy. As requirements grow, separate stable identity from mutable status and avoid using a display name as the only key. A good type reduces the number of invalid states the rest of the program must consider. checks.prompt: Why is empty stderr worth saying out loud?

checks.prompt: How should you explain exit code 0?
